top.line: Seven IAM predictions, checked against agent teams that run today
top.para: Sunnykumar K.'s predictions for 2027 to 2030 mostly describe how our agent teams already work: policies per role, keyed agent identities outnumbering the person, sealed secrets, per-wake evaluation and countable controls. I would bet differently on consolidation and on model-made access decisions.

in-short.line: Seven lines from his predictions to our bets
in-short.para: Several predictions already describe our teams; non-human identities outnumber the human 31 to 1; evaluation is per wake; the board counts Boundaries; the policy should be open; and models should advise, not decide.

seven.para: Static roles give way to policy; non-human identities reach 100 to 1; passwords disappear; IGA, CIEM and PAM consolidate; continuous evaluation becomes standard; models make access decisions; identity reaches the board.

roles.para: A role here names a written policy: what the agent may read and write, which paths it owns, what it must never do; the gate checks the policies as data, and an Agent Behaviour Policy adds what the agent is for.

nhi.para: 31 agent sessions made their own keys in two days for one person: nine for the talk, thirteen for the cold read, nine for the book; they spawn sub-agents too. Machine identity needs its own governance, and ours is a key per session, a role and a policy.

passwords.para: Secrets are sealed to a session's public key and never typed into its context; the reader's vault opens with a passkey whose PRF output computes the door to the key.

continuous.para: Each wake is planned, reviewed, worked, reviewed and checked; keys carry end dates and die with sessions; a hold file any member can pull stops every wake until the editor lifts it, as it did at 18:44 on the day of the talk.

board.line: The board wants a count of real controls
board.para: Every policy row is classified by who enforces it, and only Boundaries count; one rule in eleven was a Boundary in our own writer's policy. That is the number to report and to insure.

bets.para: Consolidation makes a policy enforceable only where one platform reaches; better an open policy read by many enforcers. Models should find anomalies and advise, but the decision that lets an agent through must stay deterministic and outside the model.

limits.para: Our teams are small and ours; the counts are this week's; the predictions are quoted from his post; I build what the article argues for.

sources.para: Sunnykumar K.'s post, shared as screenshots, and our three teams' repositories and articles.
